scenes.line2: How do Span and Memory help?
scenes.say: Ever wish your code ran faster with less garbage collection? Let's see how Span and Memory can help you cut down heap allocations.

scenes.label: Span<T>
scenes.sub: Stack-only, fast for slicing arrays or buffers.
scenes.say: Span lets you work with slices of arrays or buffers, all on the stack. That means no new heap allocations.

scenes.label: Memory<T>
scenes.sub: Works across methods and async calls.
scenes.say: Memory is like Span's flexible cousin. It can cross method and async boundaries, making it great for longer-lived data.

scenes.code:
Span<byte> slice = buffer.AsSpan(10, 20);
Memory<byte> mem = new Memory<byte>(buffer, 10, 20);
scenes.say: Here's how you create a Span for fast, in-place processing, and a Memory for async-safe data handling.

scenes.question: Can you use Span<T> in async methods?
scenes.right: No, Span is stack-only and can't cross async boundaries.
scenes.say: Careful! Span can't be used in async methods because it's stack-only. Use Memory instead when you need to await.
